title: Ave Maria (Ellens Gesang III)
description: Schubert's 1825 song from his Walter Scott settings (D. 839), later sung with the Latin Ave Maria text and one of the most famous melodies ever written. Learning it teaches singing-tone legato over a rolling triplet accompaniment and the ornamental turns of a Romantic vocal line.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: The complete first verse in the original B-flat major: two-bar piano prelude, the vocal line in the right hand with Schubert's written-out turns (grace notes realised as 32nds), the sextuplet accompaniment reduced to left-hand triplets of bass plus two chord tones, and the original three-bar postlude.
teachingPoints: Left hand: every beat is one triplet, bass note (finger 5) then two chord tones; practise it alone with a metronome until the triplets are perfectly even and quiet.
Right hand: the melody lies between G4 and F5 around Bb4-D5; keep the long notes singing and shape each ornamental turn (bars 5, 6, 9, 11) as a decoration, not a rhythm exercise.
Bar 5 has a 32nd-note pair (C-Bb) and bar 8 a sextuplet after a tie; count these bars slowly in 16ths before playing them in tempo.
Watch the accidentals: E natural in the bass of bars 3 and 7, C-sharp in bar 6, B natural in bars 7, 9 and 10, D-flat in bar 12.
Prelude and postlude (bars 1-2, 14-17): right hand plays rising dyads in triplets over left-hand octaves; keep them pp so the melody entrance in bar 3 can be the first real sound.
